text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx rate observed in control-plane. Affected endpoints: /v1/orgs/* (org-lookup), /v1/auth/token. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6.8% in the last 3m. Paging on-call.

ana (oncall): I’m on it. Seeing same in Grafana — tail latency increasing, p95 auth lookup ~1.2s and timeouts at backend. Will triage.

mike (sre): Noted. Any customer-facing errors reported?

liz (product): A few support pings. One major customer reported API failures for user provisioning. Could be impact to signups.

ana (oncall): Quick scope:
- error budget: spikes mostly 502/504 from the gateway.
- hosts: ctrlplane-eu and ctrlplane-us both impacted but eu worse.
- service traces show org-lookup RPCs timing out to billing-service cache refresh.

jess (platform): Suspect heartbeat/fanout to billing/config is stalling org-lookup paths. Suggest immediate containment: 1) enable orglookup local cache fallback 2) raise circuit-breaker threshold for org-lookup 3) throttle non-essential background refresh calls.

dan (eng-lead): Agree. We can flip cache fallback quickly via runtime feature flag. @jess do you have the flag key?

jess (platform): Flag: `runtime.features.orglookup_local_fallback` — will flip to ON in prod now. Rolling to all regions.

mike (sre): Before flipping, what's the expected consistency tradeoff? Cache TTL might serve slightly stale org metadata for up to 5m. Acceptable?

dan (eng-lead): For mitigation yes. We prefer availability. We'll run a fast revalidation job after stabilization.

ana (oncall): Doing changes:
- `runtime.features.orglookup_local_fallback` => ON
- Increase request timeout for org-lookup from `800ms` to `1500ms` in gateway (temp)
- Add 429-based backoff for billing refresh endpoints

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-4075001234 created, priority: P1, responders: ana, mike.

jess (platform): Flipped flag in eu region. Patch rollout logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z featureflag: orglookup_local_fallback=ON region=eu rollout=1/3
2026-03-15T14:12:11Z featureflag: orglookup_local_fallback=ON region=us rollout=2/3
2026-03-15T14:12:28Z featureflag: orglookup_local_fallback=ON region=ap rollout=3/3
```

ana (oncall): Gateway timeouts lowered in eu, increasing to 1500ms now.

mike (sre): Observability: within 90s of flag flip, eu 5xx dropped from 7.2% -> 2.1%. Latency p95 back down to ~420ms. US also improving but slower.

liz (product): Update for support: telling customers we saw a transient outage due to dependency timeouts and turned on cached fallback; mitigation in progress.

ana (oncall): Quick customer-impact estimate:
- ~18% of control-plane requests touched org-lookup during spike window
- overall platform error rate impacted ~2.3% of user requests globally for the 12m peak window
- critical customer incidents reported: 3 (one P2 for provisioning).

dan (eng-lead): Root cause hypothesis: billing service refresh task started a storm of cache invalidations after a malformed heartbeat, causing org-lookup RPCs to the fresh cache layer to overload the downstream DB -> timeouts -> gateway 502s.

jess (platform): Confirmed we saw a sudden burst of `cache_refresh` calls from billing workers at 14:08:xx.

mike (sre): Short-term actions (in-flight):
- keep local fallback enabled for 30m
- throttle billing refresh workers by 50% (rate limit token bucket)
- increase circuit-breaker for org-lookup to fail fast to fallback after 200ms of queueing
- apply temporary routing override to prefer us-east for new traffic while eu stabilizes

ana (oncall): Executed throttle on billing workers: `curl -X POST https://admin-api/scale?service=billing-refresh&rate=0.5` -> 200 OK.

jess (platform): Routing override active: `routeoverride set ctrlplane default_region=us-east until=15:00Z`

mike (sre): Telemetry shows error rate down to 0.9% cluster-wide now. Customer pings decreasing.

liz (product): Messaging: Prepared a brief status note for external comms. Ready to publish after we hit 1% sustained for 10m.

dan (eng-lead): For postmortem: capture the malformed heartbeat root cause, why cache refresh didn't backpressure, and add safety gate in billing worker to avoid cache storms.

ana (oncall): Handoff plan: I’ll monitor for next 45m and then hand to @mike for post-incident cleanup and followups. Current incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4075001234

pagerduty-bot: Shift handover scheduled in 45 minutes to mike (sre).

mike (sre): I’ll take over at ~15:00Z for retros and remediation. Next steps I’ll own:
- confirm DB load baseline and add a throttle at source if needed
- revert routing override once eu stabilizes for 15m
- coordinate with billing team for safer refresh gating

ana (oncall): Quick debugging logs (sample):
```
[14:08:09.123] billing-refresh worker id=br-12 event=cache_refresh keys=312 batch=128 duration=120ms
[14:08:09.456] org-lookup svc=org-lookup instance=ol-07 rpc=lookup duration=1020ms err=deadline_exceeded
[14:08:10.002] gateway route=/v1/orgs/12345 upstream=org-lookup status=502
```

jess (platform): Adding alert rule to avoid simultaneous global refresh: `alert: BillingRefreshStorm` with a 5m aggregation and suppression if rate > X.

liz (product): I’ll sync with support to escalate the one provisioning P2 and provide timeline.

dan (eng-lead): Good containment. After stabilization, we should run an exercise to simulate similar refresh storms in staging.

ana (oncall): Status: moving to monitoring-only. If 5xx < 1% for 10m, we set incident to resolved and create follow-up ticket list.

mike (sre): A note for post-incident actions:
- remediation ticket: RB-4075001 (billing refresh gating)
- infra change: RB-4075002 (orglookup cb tuning and fallback as default)
- runbook update: add explicit steps to enable local fallback and routing override

ana (oncall): Thanks all. I’ll leave the incident in watch and will ping if any regression. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-4075001234 status: monitoring.
